meta.title: Advisories: Cybercrime Report & Track
meta.description: General, evergreen advisories on common cybercrime patterns in India, without invented statistics or incident data.

title: Advisories
subtitle: Recognisable patterns behind common scams, written to stay true regardless of the date. Nothing here is a live incident feed, and no numbers are invented.
heroImageAlt: A person reading a newspaper, held up in front of their face.

items.title: Digital arrest and fake law-enforcement calls
items.body: A caller claims to be from the police, customs, CBI, or a court, says a parcel or your Aadhaar is linked to a crime, and pressures you to stay on a video call and transfer money to "clear your name." Real Indian law enforcement does not arrest, investigate, or collect fines over a phone or video call.

items.title: KYC update and bank-verification scams
items.body: A message or call claims your bank account, UPI, or SIM will be blocked unless you "update KYC" immediately through a link or by sharing an OTP. Banks never ask for your OTP, PIN, or password to update KYC. Go directly to your bank's app or branch instead.

items.title: Investment and trading scams
items.body: A WhatsApp or Telegram group promises guaranteed returns, often showing fake screenshots of other members' profits, and pushes you toward a trading app or website outside official channels. Verify any advisor or platform against SEBI's registered-intermediary list before sending money.

items.title: Fake job and work-from-home offers
items.body: An offer promises easy pay for simple tasks, like liking videos or rating products, but asks you to pay a small "registration" or "activation" fee first, or asks you to invest earnings to unlock withdrawals. A genuine job never asks you to pay to get paid.

items.title: Loan-app harassment
items.body: Unregulated lending apps offer instant loans with minimal checks, then use excessive permissions granted during installation (contacts, photos) to harass the borrower and their contacts over repayment. Use only RBI-regulated lenders and read app permissions before installing.

items.title: SIM swap fraud
items.body: A fraudster gathers enough of your personal details to convince your telecom operator to reissue your number on a new SIM, then uses it to intercept OTPs. Sudden, unexplained loss of mobile signal for an extended period is a warning sign worth acting on immediately.

items.title: Phishing links over SMS and WhatsApp
items.body: A message claiming to be a courier, electricity board, or bank sends a shortened link to a fake login page that captures your credentials. Check the sender and the actual domain of any link before entering details anywhere.

footer: This list describes recurring patterns, not today's incidents. See our <link>Cyber Safety Tips</link> for the actions to take before and after something happens.
